authorFinding.title: Unvalidated name interpolated into a path and run through sh -c (sibling of the unconfined-path-read seeds)
authorFinding.failureScenario: If an untrusted caller can supply `name` to run(), the shape matches the seeds: an unvalidated name is spliced into a file path and nothing confines it to /srv/data. Here the splice goes into a shell string passed to `sh -c`. name="../../etc/passwd" would read outside /srv/data. name="x; id" or "$(...)" would run arbitrary commands, which is worse than the seeds' file read. Reachability is not established. run is a private fn, and no supplied file calls it. Whether `name` is attacker-controlled is unknown. This is a different sink class (command injection) from the JS fs.readFile seeds, with the same root cause of unvalidated input reaching a file-path sink. Not executed.
authorFinding.action: Do not build a shell string. Use Command::new("cat").arg("--").arg(path) as the clean variant does. Reject names containing ".." or '/', or canonicalize the path and check it stays under /srv/data. Confirm whether any caller outside the supplied files passes untrusted input to run().

findings.reason: In the planted file, `name` goes unchecked into a shell command string that is run through `sh -c`, so the shell parses it. Nothing confines the path to /srv/data. Whether an attacker can reach `run` is not in the packet, so the candidate's own 'speculative' confidence and low severity are appropriate.
